your_book:
Jaleel's book had a mixed Friday session against a backdrop of falling yields and declining oil prices. The clearest winners were NVDA (+1.34%) and AVGO (+2.97%), both lifted by broad chip-sector strength and market optimism around U.S. manufacturing talks between Intel and SK Hynix. ABT edged up +0.37% and AZO added +0.39%, providing quiet ballast. On the software side, headlines suggested AI-growth skepticism from Anthropic, OpenAI, and SpaceXAI executives could ease competitive pressure on incumbents — yet ADBE still slipped -1.48% and SAP fell -1.97%, meaning the narrative tailwind didn't translate into Friday gains for either name.

The sharpest drag came from RKLB, down -4.79% on a day when Bitcoin topped $80,000 and the S&P slipped as yields reclaimed 5% — classic risk-off pressure on a speculative, cash-burning name already rated AVOID with a QARP score of just 39.0 and a -17.6% unrealized loss. ZTS fell -2.22% with no specific catalyst visible, pushing its loss to -9.3%; NBIX dropped -3.69%, deepening its drawdown to -10.3%. BSX continued to drift lower (-0.48%), now -11.6% in the hole after its guidance slash.

The thesis-vs-price divergence to watch most closely is LULU, now -23.3% unrealized with a guidance cut on record and Americas comps still running negative — yet the system rates it STRONG BUY. BSX carries a similar tension: STRONG BUY verdict, but management guided flat through Q3. RKLB is the starkest mismatch of all: an AVOID rating sitting at nearly 7% of the book. The pharma cluster (GILD, NVS, NBIX, VRTX) carries a policy overhang from MFN pricing deals that isn't fully priced into verdicts. Next hard dates: ABT on Oct 13, BSX on Oct 28.

attention.headline: AVOID-rated at ~7% weight, -17.6% loss, -4.79% today
attention.note: Rocket Lab carries the book's lowest QARP (39.0), an explicit AVOID verdict, and is now the sixth-largest position — a capital-preservation mandate is hard to square with that combination, and today's selloff on rising yields makes it worse.

attention.note: Price and thesis are visibly diverging — the STRONG BUY verdict has not been validated by fundamentals (tariff margin hit, China stalled, FY guide cut), and the next catalyst isn't until Dec 9, leaving the position exposed for months.

attention.note: Management's own guidance (FY26 growth cut to 7–8.5%, flat through Q3) conflicts with the STRONG BUY rating; Oct 28 earnings will be the first real read on whether the thesis is recovering or deteriorating.
